# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** Pompey Storms Jerusalem; God Strikes Him Down

---

**2:1** In his insolence the sinner smashed down the strong walls —
and you, O God, did nothing to stop him.

**2:2** Foreign nations climbed your altar;
they stamped it down with contemptuous boots.

**2:3** Because Jerusalem's own sons had already defiled the LORD's holy things,
had fouled God's offerings with their own wickedness.

**2:4** Because of this God declared: 'Away — remove these things from my sight';
his glory meant nothing to them.

**2:5** Jerusalem's children mocked the holy things of God,
shamed his offerings with their lawless hands.

**2:6** Therefore God declared: 'Put them far away —
they have not honored my holiness anywhere.'

**2:7** The conqueror stood proudly on their heights
and showed no mercy.

**2:8** He battered down the walls with his rams;
God, you did not hold him back.

**2:9** The foreigners marched up to your altar;
they ground it under their heels in contempt.

**2:10** Because Jerusalem's sons had defiled the LORD's sanctuary,
had profaned what was holy to God.

**2:11** He drove their sons and daughters into grinding captivity —
collars around their necks, a shameful spectacle for all the nations.

**2:12** God dealt with them according to their own sins;
he handed them over to the power of those who crushed them.

**2:13** He turned his face away — refused to show them pity;
young men and young women, dragged away into exile.

**2:14** In the bloom of their youth they marched away before the enemy;
and I cried out to the LORD God:

**2:15** 'Be just, O LORD, in every judgment you render —
your righteousness stands from age to age.'

**2:16** Your judgments reach across all the earth in equity;
whoever does not know you gets taught by your hand.

**2:17** You have tested us like silver in the furnace,
you have searched our kidneys and our hearts.

**2:18** You stretched out your hand over us
and rescued us from the ones who oppressed us.

**2:19** You lit our lamp, O LORD our God;
our feet walk on your righteous paths.

**2:20** We will call upon the LORD forever —
let all nations know: God reigns over Israel!

**2:21** For I watched this man raise his fist against the holy city
with insolence and contempt.

**2:22** He slaughtered their sons, violated their daughters;
he poured out innocent blood like water around Jerusalem.

**2:23** He herded the young men off into slavery,
and Jerusalem's daughters into defilement.

**2:24** He mocked them before the nations;
yet God repaid the sinners in exact measure for what they had done.

**2:25** He shamed the body of God's anointed;
he shed that blood with arrogant hands.

**2:26** Then God laid bare the crimes of this insolent man before all the earth —
exposed him before all peoples.

**2:27** He dashed him on the rocks of Egypt,
a humiliation greater than any Egypt had ever known.

**2:28** His body rolled in the waves, tossed about in contempt —
no one buried him, for God had cast him away in disgust.

**2:29** He never stopped to think that he was only a man,
never considered where his road would end.

**2:30** He boasted: 'I will rule land and sea!' —
never grasping that God is great,
great and mighty beyond all measuring.

**2:31** He is the King of heaven itself,
who passes judgment on kings and powers.

**2:32** He lifts me up to glory;
he brings the arrogant crashing down to ruin forever.

**2:33** As for me — I will cry out to the mighty God,
with a heart full of praise.

**2:34** I will sing you praises, O God, among the poor who are gathered;
for you are the joy and the crown of all who fear you.

**2:35** Praise to the LORD in all his ways;
for his judgments are righteous and holy.

**2:36** For he keeps faith with his servants
and shows compassion to the humble.

**2:37** Blessed is the one who fears the LORD —
God's own hand will deliver him.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic rendering prioritizing poetic force and contemporary resonance. Sense-for-sense.*
